current_activity: a task force of about fifteen Panthers and two infantry battalions strikes the French at Châtel in a pincers attack
notes: Event date: late afternoon of 16 September 1944 (Cole, ch. 4). Event definition: Late on 16 September a large task force from the brigade strikes Châtel, held by Leclerc's troops across the Moselle, in a pincers attack and is beaten off (Cole, ch. 4); Wikipedia: sent to Remiremont on 6 September, under the XXXXVII Corps. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 4, p. 204: "a large task force from the 111th Panzer Brigade (estimated to consist of fifteen Panthers and two infantry battalions) suddenly struck Châtel in a pincers attack"; Wikipedia, List of German brigades in World War II: "Placed under command of XXXXVII Corps in September 1944". Location: Châtel-sur-Moselle, Vosges (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Châtel. Commander: Colonel Heinrich Bronsart von Schellendorf (Cole, ch. 5). Opponents: French 2nd Armored Division.

current_activity: Mark IVs and 88s from its reserve block Abrams's CCA drive on Hill 260 and Hill 241 west of Ommeray, near Ley
notes: Event date: 20 September 1944 (Cole, ch. 5). Event definition: As CCA, 4th Armored Division, drives on Ley on 20 September, a group of Mark IV tanks and 88-mm. guns from the brigade reserve takes position on Hills 260 and 241 west of Ommeray and stops C Company, 37th Tank Battalion; the added armour of the brigade prevents a clear decision (Cole, ch. 5). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 228: "a group of Mark IV tanks and 88-mm. guns from the 111th Panzer Brigade reserve to positions on Hill 260 and Hill 241 west of Ommeray"; Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 229: "the additional armored weight given the LVIII Panzer Corps by the 111th Panzer Brigade prevented any clear-cut decision". Location: Ley, Moselle (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Ley, Ommeray and Hills 260 and 241. Commander: Colonel Heinrich Bronsart von Schellendorf (Cole, ch. 5). Opponents: US 4th Armored Division (CCA).

current_activity: attack toward Juvelize and Moyenvic is shot to pieces; commander mortally wounded, seven tanks and eighty men left
notes: Event date: 22 September 1944 (Cole, ch. 5). Event definition: The brigade attacks toward Juvelize, three hours late, against the 25th Cavalry Squadron and CCA; fourteen tanks are destroyed east of Juvelize, Colonel Bronsart von Schellendorf is mortally wounded, and only seven tanks and eighty men are left (Cole, ch. 5; Wikipedia, Battle of Arracourt). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 231: "commander of the 111th Panzer Brigade, was mortally"; Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 232: "Only seven tanks and eighty men were left in the 111th Panzer"; Wikipedia, Battle of Arracourt: "the 11th Panzer Division and the 111th and 113th Panzer Brigades". Location: Juvelize, Moselle with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Juvelize. Commander: Colonel Heinrich Bronsart von Schellendorf (Cole, ch. 5). Opponents: US 4th Armored Division (CCA, 25th Cavalry Squadron).
